question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation, delegation, and volitional compaction as a disabled-by-default first-party agent lifecycle feature with trusted internal return events?
rationale: The PR creates new config, protocol, plugin SDK, persisted state, session lifecycle, and security-boundary behavior, so automation cannot decide whether this belongs in core or what exact proof bar maintainers require.

options.title: Require proof and signoff before merge
options.body: Keep the feature direction open but require a conflict-free head, maintainer product/security approval, and exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, and request_compaction success before landing.

options.title: Accept as experimental opt-in
options.body: Merge the default-off design while maintainers explicitly own the remaining upgrade, proof, and trusted-return boundary risk.

options.title: Split or defer
options.body: Pause this PR and ask for smaller owner-reviewed slices that separate config/schema, continuation tools, delegate routing, compaction behavior, and observability.

recommendation.title: Require proof and signoff before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction open but require a conflict-free head, maintainer product/security approval, and exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, and request_compaction success before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/API direction choice for core agent lifecycle behavior, and Peter Steinberger is the strongest available product-owner signal from current history and maintainer routing.
